changes: Content of the first reading kept as is; notes expanded: why 'dayakā' gives the commissioner role, how 'sumati jaya' is taken as royal epithets, the uncertain phrase 'oguli chātasa hleyā', and the catalogue's place and date fields.

notes: The colophon reads samvat 802 (NS, about 1682 CE). The catalogue gives NS 815 (about 1695 CE). Both years fall within Jitāmitra Malla's reign in Bhaktapur (about 1673–1696). This is item (2) of a multi-text reel, so the catalogue's 815 may come from another colophon in the same bundle. 'śuddhi' is taken as the bright half (śukla). 'sumati jaya' is read as part of the king's royal style (epithets), not as his personal name. The commissioner role rests on Newari '-sana dayakā' ('made by'). It does not say whether he commissioned only this copy or the ritual it records. 'oguli chātasa hleyā' is unclear. It may mean 'written/offered on these leaves' or refer to the occasion. No scribe is named. The place, Bhaktapur, comes only from the catalogue field. It fits Jitāmitra's kingdom but is not stated in the colophon, so it is left empty.
